title: Flat-object small-etale to big-fppf derived section comparison
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] on the small etale site, equivalently on its enlarged model [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Choose a small big site $\mathcal B_X$ of algebraic spaces over $X$, containing the spaces and fibre products under consideration, in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Its coverings are jointly surjective families of flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms (these properties are tested on etale scheme charts); its ring sheaf is $\mathcal O(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Put $F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,h^*F)$ for $h:T\to X$, with restriction by tensor pullback. This presheaf is an fppf sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F^a\to J^\bullet$ be an injective resolution, with $J^q=0$ for $q<0$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every flat $h:T\to X$ there is a canonical isomorphism in the derived category of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},h^*F)\ \simeq\ J^\bullet(T).$$
For $T=X$ it is the usual small-etale to big-fppf comparison. These isomorphisms are natural for flat morphisms $T'\to T$ over $X$, including maps to $X$, with the maps on the right induced by restriction in the single resolution $J^\bullet$. More precisely, for every small augmented diagram of such flat $X$-spaces with flat arrows, they identify the diagrams of derived sections before taking cohomology: compatible resolution models for the small-etale derived sections are connected to the diagram $T\mapsto J^\bullet(T)$ by face-compatible zigzags of componentwise quasi-isomorphisms of complexes, uniformly bounded below by zero. The augmentation maps are the usual pullback/restriction maps under these identifications. No quasi-compactness or separatedness is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0DGN, lemma-review-quasi-coherent (1), (3), (6), (7), and 0DGP, lemma-cohomological-descent-etale-fppf-modules. Derived-section and flat-diagram naturality formulation supplied by the agent; no hypercover is involved.

proof.text: For an fppf cover $\{V_i\to V\}$ and compatible sections of $(h^*F)|_{V_i}$, regard each section as a map $\mathcal O_{V_i}\to(h^*F)|_{V_i}$. Full faithfulness in quasi-coherent fppf descent glues these maps uniquely to $\mathcal O_V\to h^*F$. Thus $F^a$ is a sheaf; scalar multiplication and restrictions glue because the same uniqueness applies to sums and scalar multiples. Tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence. For every $h:T\to X$, put $F_T=h^*F$. On the slice $\mathcal B_X/T$, the restriction of $F^a$ equals $F_T^a$: at $v:V\to T$ both are $\Gamma(V,(hv)^*F)$, using the canonical tensor associator, which respects units and composition.

source.place: Tag 0DGN, lemma-review-quasi-coherent, proof of (1); pullback composition in the definition of F^a

proof.text: Write $j_T$ for localization to $\mathcal B_X/T$ and $J_T=j_T^*J$. Exact module restriction makes $F_T^a\to J_T$ a nonnegative resolution. Moreover $j_T^*$ preserves injectives: it is the right adjoint of the exact extension-by-zero functor $j_{T!}$. Thus $J_T$ is an injective resolution on the big site over $T$. This uses localization at an arbitrary site object, not an open immersion of schemes. All module categories here have enough injectives: apply the small module-diagram Grothendieck theorem with the terminal index category, then the enough-injectives theorem.

source.place: Tag 03DJ, exact extension by zero and its restriction adjunction; ringed localization to the object T

proof.text: Let $a_T$ be the big-fppf to small-etale ringed morphism, and set $K_T=a_{T,*}J_T$. The new higher-vanishing lemma applies to $F_T$, since it is quasi-coherent by step 1. Consequently $H^i(K_T)=R^ia_{T,*}F_T^a=0$ for $i>0$. In degree zero, restriction to an etale $v:V\to T$ gives, since by the localization clause of the enlarged etale model tensor pullback along an etale map is restriction, $F_T^a(V)=\Gamma(V,v^*F_T)=F_T(V)$; hence the augmentation is a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism $F_T[0]\to K_T$. The construction is nonnegative, and on every enlarged etale object $V/T$ it has the explicit formula $K_T^q(V)=J^q(V)$, with the same differentials.

source.place: Tag 0DGN, lemma-review-quasi-coherent (7); (6) is the degree-zero restriction identity, written out here

proof.text: Each term of $K_T$ is the module direct image by $a_T$ of the injective module $J_T^q$. The injective-pushforward theorem makes it totally acyclic, in particular acyclic for global sections. Apply acyclic-resolution derived computation to $F_T[0]\to K_T$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $Q\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},K_T)\cong R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},F_T)$ in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$. Since $\Gamma(T,K_T)=J^\bullet(T)$ term by term, its inverse is the required comparison. This also covers $T=X$ with the identity augmentation and the same original resolution.

For $g:T'\to T$ over $X$, define $K_T\to g_*K_{T'}$ on an enlarged etale object $V/T$ by the restriction $J^\bullet(V)\to J^\bullet(V\times_TT')$. Use the enlarged small-site model so the fibre product is an allowed etale algebraic-space object; on scheme charts this is the ordinary module direct image. The map is linear over $\mathcal O_T$ and commutes with differentials. On augmentations it is exactly $F_T\to g_*F_{T'}$ induced by tensor pullback, by the formula of step 1. Derived-map computation for acyclic resolutions therefore identifies its section map $J^\bullet(T)\to J^\bullet(T')$ with the usual coefficient-compatible derived restriction. Thus this equality is in the derived category, not merely an equality on the groups $H^i$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, applied to the explicit section restriction maps

proof.text: For any of the stated small augmented diagrams, take $K_T$ as the compatible small-etale acyclic resolution models. Every map on their sections is the corresponding restriction in $J$. Restrictions for a composite equal the composite restrictions, and identities act identically, since $J$ is a complex of sheaves on one site. Hence these section complexes form the strict diagram $T\mapsto J^\bullet(T)$, including its augmentation, and the zigzag to that diagram can be the identity map of this chosen model. All components are zero below degree zero. Step 5 identifies every arrow with the specified derived restriction, so this is a simultaneous comparison of the entire diagram. No finite bound on the number of objects or faces, and no quasi-compactness or separatedness, was used.
